item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-03
item.description: On 2026-11-02 the Wuzhen Summit opened under a theme in which the word open source appears for the first time in twelve years of the conference: 'Open Source and Openness, Joint Contribution and Shared Benefits.' The same day, the World Internet Conference's AI Professional Committee held its annual plenary and approved its 2027 plan, whose one operative sentence is that the committee will 'actively promote the transformation of the open-source openness initiative into action' (积极推进开源开放倡议转化为行动). Read together with the objects the summit has actually built — a first-ever open-source-themed experience hall in the World Internet Science and Technology Museum, an open-source track in the Straight to Wuzhen competition, a Wuzhen Talk open-source youth forum opened to public booking, and 1,000-plus achievements across 671 exhibitors from 54 countries — the picture is of a state promoting open source as a norm it issues rather than a repository it publishes. The instrument is the summit theme and the committee work plan; the missing instrument is a licence, a deposit, or an access rule. Ant Group's contribution to the opening of the experience hall states the ambition in its own words: 'we look forward to open source becoming the basic public good of the digital world' — a claim about a commons made by a firm, in a hall built by a conference, in a country whose largest open-source foundation runs on membership dues rather than endowments.
